newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek securities watchdog fines Delta Securities.
newsitem.headline: Greek securities watchdog fines Delta Securities.

text.p: Greece's capital market commission imposed fines totalling 1.5 billion drachmas on Athens bourse member Delta Securities and three individuals for manipulative trading in the shares of Magrizos.
The commission said it also fined Panagiotis Tryfon 700 million drachmas, Angelo Dikos 100 million and Demosthenes Tzanis 100 million.
Its decision was based on the findings of an audit conducted by three international auditing firms it retained after the Delta Securities scandal broke late last year.
"Mr. Tryfon headed a group of individuals including Mr. Dikos and Mr. Tzanis who had numerous transactions on shares of Magrizos and Parnassos, totalling 8.0 billion drachmas," the commission said.
It said their trades sought to manipulate the market in these shares in terms of pricing, supply and demand.
Moreover, the above named individuals were conducting prearranged trades based on confidential information which is a serious violation of existing regulations.
The commission said Delta Securities was actively involved in these trades and provided all three with financing arrangements.
"It should be noted that during the 10-day period prior to Delta's default with the clearing house, the Tryfon-led group's trades made up 50 percent of the firm's turnover," the commission said.
The close examination of the audit findings is continuing, it said.
